In what year was Klinefelter syndrome discovered?
Klinefelter syndrome (KS), also known as 47,XXY, is a chromosome anomaly.
Bash (Unix shell): Brian Fox. Bash (short for "Bourne Again SHell") is an interactive command interpreter and command language developed for Unix-like operating systems.
Airbus A220: Bombardier Aerospace. The Airbus A220 is a family of five-abreast narrow-body airliners by Airbus Canada Limited Partnership (ACLP).
Cannoli: Italy. Cannoli are Sicilian pastries consisting of a tube-shaped shell of fried pastry dough, filled with a sweet and creamy filling containing ricotta cheese.
Who is credited with discovering Copernicium?
GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research
Copernicium: GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research. Copernicium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Cn and atomic number 112.
Who is credited with discovering Pluto?
Pluto: Clyde Tombaugh. Pluto (minor-planet number 134340) is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt, a ring of bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
Who is credited with discovering Influenza A virus?
Influenza A virus: Christopher Andrewes. Influenza A virus, or IAV, is a pathogen with strains that cause seasonal flu in humans; it can also infect birds and some mammals.
Heading Switzerland's Federal Department of Home Affairs for over a decade, this politician succeeded Marija Pejčinović Burić atop a major European institution in 2024 — who is he?
Alain Berset (French; born 9 April 1972) is a Swiss politician who served as a Member of the Swiss Federal Council from 2012 to 2023.
Struck off the medical register for the fraudulent 1998 Lancet paper that falsely tied the MMR vaccine to autism, this former surgeon sparked a plunge in vaccination rates — who is he?
Andrew Wakefield (born 3 September 1956) is an English fraudster, anti-vaccine activist, and former senior surgeon.
This mid-sized zodiac constellation, sitting between Pisces and Taurus, has represented a ram since late Babylonian times — though its stars once formed a farmhand. Which one is it?
Aries (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac. It is located in the Northern celestial hemisphere between Pisces to the west and Taurus to the east.
Nicknamed 'Red-Stockings,' this French herding dog breed hails from the plains of Central France — which breed is it?
Beauceron (French) is a herding dog breed originating from the plains of Central France.
Composed mostly of plasma along with red cells, white cells, and platelets, this body fluid ferries oxygen and nutrients to cells while hauling waste away — name the fluid?

Blood is a body fluid in the circulatory system of humans and other vertebrates that delivers necessary substances such as nutrients and oxygen to the cells of the body, and transports metabolic waste products away from those same cells.

This opioid medication used to treat addiction and pain can be delivered under the tongue, through the cheek, by injection, patch, or implant — and is often combined with naloxone to deter misuse — what drug is it?
Buprenorphine is an opioid used to treat opioid use disorder, acute pain, and chronic pain.
Named for its habit of burrowing nests into dead wood or bamboo, this genus of some 500 bee species includes one soil-tunneling exception among its 31 subgenera — what insect is it?
Carpenter bee are species in the genus Xylocopa of the subfamily Xylocopinae.
Originating in Northern China, this spitz-type dog breed is known for a dense double coat that forms a distinctive ruff around the neck — name the breed?
Chow Chow is a spitz-type of dog breed originally from Northern China.
Scholars still argue whether it merely transmits meaning or also creates it, but the simplest definition of this concept is the transmission of information — what is it?
Communication is commonly defined as the transmission of information.
Native to Mexico and Central America and related to the sunflower and daisy, this genus of 49 tuberous perennial species blooms in nearly every color except blue — which genus?
Dahlia is a genus of bushy, tuberous, herbaceous perennial plants native to Mexico and Central America.
A member of the catecholamine family made by stripping a carboxyl group from L-DOPA, this brain chemical is central to reward-motivated behavior — what is it?
Dopamine (DA, a contraction of 3,4-dihydroxyphenethylamine) is a neuromodulatory molecule that plays several important roles in cells.
Not a single disease but a syndrome of overall brain dysfunction with many possible causes, this term's Greek roots literally mean 'brain suffering' — what is it called?
Encephalopathy (from Ancient Greek (enkphalos) 'brain' and (pthos) 'suffering') is any disorder or disease of the brain, especially chronic degenerative conditions.
What is the scientific term for the solid waste material left after digestion, discharged through the anus, and sometimes reused as fertilizer, fuel, or building material?
Feces (also faeces or fces or poop) are the solid or semi-solid remains of food that was not digested in the small intestine, and has been broken down by bacteria in the large intestine.
This Austrian-school economist shared the 1974 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences with Gunnar Myrdal for work on how prices communicate information — who is he?
Friedrich Hayek (8 May 1899 - 23 March 1992) was an Austrian economist and philosopher.
One of Europe's smallest songbirds, this kinglet sports a bright orange-and-yellow crest in males and closely resembles the firecrest — which bird?
Goldcrest (Regulus regulus) is a very small passerine bird in the kinglet family.
This daisy-family genus native to North America and Mexico includes the common sunflower and the Jerusalem artichoke among its roughly 50 species — which genus?
Helianthus is a genus comprising around 50 species of annual and perennial flowering plants in the daisy family Asteraceae commonly known as sunflowers.
With atomic number 1, this element's most common isotope holds just one proton and one electron, and it's what stars like the Sun mainly burn — what is it?
Hydrogen is a chemical element; it has the symbol H and atomic number 1.
Its name comes from the Ancient Greek for 'violet,' fitting for an element that boils into a violet gas — and it sits at atomic number 53 as the heaviest stable halogen. What is it?
Iodine is a chemical element; it has symbol I and atomic number 53.
Two years after unveiling the first mechanical television system, this Scottish engineer achieved the first-ever transatlantic television transmission in 1928 — who is he?
John Logie Baird (13 August 1888 - 14 June 1946) was a Scottish inventor, electrical engineer and innovator who demonstrated the world's first mechanical television system on 26 January 1926.
Striking children as they wean, up to about age five, this protein-deficiency disorder produces edema and a fatty, enlarged liver — what is it called?
Kwashiorkor (-kr) is a form of severe protein malnutrition characterized by edema and an enlarged liver with fatty infiltrates.
Popular in aquariums but a destructive invader in the Atlantic and Mediterranean, this venomous Indo-Pacific creature warns predators off with bold red and black stripes — what is it?
Lionfish (genus Pterois) are venomous marine fish native to the Indo-Pacific.
Domesticated in southern Mexico about 9,000 years ago from wild teosinte, this grain was grown by Native Americans alongside beans and squash in the 'Three Sisters' method — name the tall grass crop?
Maize (Zea mays), also known as corn, is a tall stout grass that produces cereal grain.
Triggered by falling progesterone, this monthly discharge from the uterine lining signals that pregnancy hasn't occurred and typically first arrives at "menarche" between ages 11 and 13 — what is it?
Menstruation (also known as a period, among other colloquial terms) is the regular discharge of blood and mucosal tissue from the inner lining of the uterus through the vagina.
Also called a mutt, this designation covers any dog outside official breed standards — with an estimated 150 million examples worldwide, believed to enjoy 'hybrid vigor' — what's it called?
Mongrel is any dog which does not belong to one officially recognized breed.
This silvery lanthanide, found in the minerals monazite and bastnäsite, is about as common as cobalt or nickel despite its 'rare earth' label — which element?
Neodymium is a chemical element; it has symbol Nd and atomic number 60.
This Persian polymath and poet was the first to provide a general geometric solution to all third-degree polynomial equations, using the intersection of conic sections. Who is he?
Omar Khayyam (1048-1131) was a Persian poet and polymath, known for his contributions to mathematics, astronomy, philosophy, and Persian literature.
Designed by Niklaus Wirth to encourage structured programming and named after a French mathematician-philosopher, this language was developed in the pattern of ALGOL 60 — name it?

Pascal (programming language) is an imperative and procedural programming language, designed by Niklaus Wirth as a small, efficient language intended to encourage good programming practices using structured programming and data structuring.
Its name comes from the Greek for 'love of wisdom,' and physics and psychology were once branches of it — what is this rational inquiry into existence and knowledge?

Philosophy (from Ancient Greek philosophia, lit. 'love of wisdom') is a systematic study of general and fundamental questions concerning topics like existence, knowledge, mind, reason, language, and value.
Abundant throughout the plant kingdom, this broad class of naturally occurring phenolic compounds includes flavonoids and ellagitannin — what is the family called?
Polyphenol are a large family of naturally occurring phenols.
Which industry has expanded from traditional books and newspapers to e-books, websites, and video games, with giants like Thomson Reuters and News Corp among its biggest players?
Publishing is the process of making information, literature, music, software, and other content, whether in physical or digital form, available to the public for sale or free of charge.
This positive-sense RNA virus in the Enterovirus genus is the most common viral infectious agent in humans and the leading cause of the common cold — name the virus?
Rhinovirus (from the Ancient) is a positive-sense, single-stranded RNA virus belonging to the genus Enterovirus in the family Picornaviridae.
This Harvard political scientist argued in a 1993 theory that future conflict would erupt not between countries but between cultures — a 'clash of civilizations.' Who was he?
Samuel P. Huntington (April 18, 1927 - December 24, 2008) was an American political scientist, adviser, and academic.

This medical state of insufficient blood flow to body tissues comes in four main types, from hypovolemic to cardiogenic, and can progress from weakness and rapid breathing to confusion or cardiac arrest. What is this condition called?
Shock (circulatory) is the state of insufficient blood flow to the tissues of the body as a result of problems with the circulatory system.
First described in 1780, this slender, long-legged antelope of southern Africa wears a white face crossed by a dark stripe from eye to mouth — and both sexes sport backward-curving horns. What is it?
Springbok (Antidorcas marsupialis) is an antelope found mainly in south and southwest Africa.

This genus of about a dozen woody flowering shrubs in the olive family, native from southeastern Europe to East Asia, is closely related to privet and provides food for several moth larvae — what is it commonly called?
Syringa is a genus of 12 currently recognized species of flowering woody plants in the olive family called lilacs.
This genus of roughly 350 species of aromatic Mediterranean herbs is the source of a common culinary seasoning that shares its name — what is the genus?
Thymus (plant) (thymes) contains about 350 species of aromatic perennial herbaceous plants and subshrubs in the family Lamiaceae.
Named from the Greek word for 'cheese' after being first isolated from milk protein in 1846, this standard amino acid is more water-loving than its close relative phenylalanine. Name the amino acid?
Tyrosine (symbol Tyr or Y) or 4-hydroxyphenylalanine is one of the 20 standard amino acids that are used by cells to synthesize proteins.
The largest bird of prey on the Australian continent, distinguished by long broad wings, fully feathered legs, and an unmistakable wedge-shaped tail. What is it?
Wedge-tailed eagle (Aquila audax) is the largest bird of prey in the continent of Australia.
Discovered in 1807 and named for the Roman goddess of home and hearth, this is thought to be the second-largest asteroid and the only known rocky protoplanet still intact in the belt — which one?
4 Vesta: Second largest main-belt asteroid. Vesta (minor-planet designation: 4 Vesta) is one of the largest objects in the asteroid belt, with a mean diameter of 525 kilometres (326 mi).
Native to sub-Saharan grasslands and woodlands, this animal is the largest living land species, with the largest recorded specimen standing nearly 13 feet tall at the shoulder — which species is it?
African bush elephant: Species of mammal. Its skin is grey with scanty hairs, and bending cracks which support thermoregulation by retaining water.

This exaggerated immune response occurs when the body mistakes a harmless substance for a threat, triggering histamine release from mast cells and conditions like hay fever or anaphylaxis. What is this reaction called?
Allergy: Immune system response to a substance that most people tolerate well.
This cosmopolitan family of water birds, found on every continent but Antarctica, groups together the ducks, geese, and swans — what is it?
Anatidae: Biological family of water birds. The family has a cosmopolitan distribution, occurring on all the world's continents except Antarctica.
Most often caused by stroke or head trauma, this condition impairs a person's ability to understand or produce language because specific brain regions aren't working. What is it?
Aphasia: Inability to comprehend or formulate language.
Larger than a meteoroid but smaller than a planet, most of these rocky, metallic, or icy bodies orbit between Mars and Jupiter — what are they called?
Asteroid: Minor planet found within the inner Solar System.
Named from a Greek word meaning 'heavy,' this soft silvery alkaline earth metal with atomic number 56 wasn't isolated until 1808 via electrolysis, decades after being identified — which element?
Barium: Chemical element with atomic number 56 (Ba)
Also called the bearcat, this dark, shaggy, tree-dwelling Asian viverrid sports a prehensile tail and musk glands that famously smell of buttered popcorn — what is it?
Binturong: Asian mammal also known as a bearcat.
Developed from a wide-body airliner and selected in 2011 to replace an aging fleet of aerial tankers, this refueling aircraft entered US Air Force service in 2019 — which aircraft?
Boeing KC-46 Pegasus: American military aerial refueling and transport aircraft.
Native to Australia and naturally green and yellow with black scalloped markings, this small, long-tailed parrot is one of the world's most popular pet birds — what is it?
Encompassing wolves, dogs, coyotes, and golden jackals, which genus is defined by its members' massive skulls, long legs, and comparatively short ears and tails?
Canis: Genus of canines. Canis is a genus of the Caninae which includes multiple extant species, such as wolves, dogs, coyotes, and golden jackals.
Native to Madagascar, this flowering plant known as the Madagascar periwinkle is the source of two major cancer-fighting drugs — what is it?
Catharanthus roseus: Species of flowering plant in the family Apocynaceae.
Domesticated from the red junglefowl roughly 8,000 years ago, this bird now numbers over 26 billion worldwide, more than any other domesticated species — what is it?
Chicken: Domesticated subspecies of red junglefowl. The chicken (Gallus gallus domesticus) is the domesticated form of the red junglefowl (Gallus gallus), originally native to Southeast Asia.
Sold under the brand name Anafranil, this tricyclic antidepressant treats obsessive-compulsive disorder but also premature ejaculation and the cataplexy that comes with narcolepsy — which drug?
Clomipramine: Antidepressant. It has also been notably used to treat premature ejaculation and the cataplexy associated with narcolepsy.
The heaviest songbird on Earth and the most widely distributed of all the corvids, this all-black passerine averages 25 inches long across the Northern Hemisphere — what is it?
Common raven: Large, black species of passerine bird.

This academic framework examines how systemic bias against certain ethnic groups is embedded in laws and institutions, using the concept of intersectionality to explain overlapping forms of inequality — what is it called?
Critical race theory: Conceptual framework. The word critical in the name is an academic reference to critical theory, not criticizing or blaming individuals.

Dubbed the 'father of modern experimental optics,' this Scottish inventor discovered the angle and the photoelasticity that bear on polarized light — and improved the stereoscope along the way. Who was he?
David Brewster: British astronomer and mathematician (1781–1868)
Sold as Benadryl, this first-generation H1-antihistamine is famously sedating — yet at higher doses it can paradoxically cause agitation and restlessness instead of sleep; what's the drug?
Diphenhydramine: Antihistamine medication. Diphenhydramine, sold under the brand name Benadryl among others, is an antihistamine and sedative.
Known medically as cerumen, this waxy secretion in the ear canal protects against bacteria, fungi, and water while trapping dust and dead skin — what is it?
Earwax: Waxy substance secreted by the ear.

Distinguished by its massive head, huge size, and trademark black facial mask, this gentle British dog breed is now classed as vulnerable in its homeland, with just 104 UK births recorded in 2020 — which breed?
English Mastiff: British breed of dog. The English Mastiff, or simply the Mastiff, is a British breed of very large dog of mastiff type.
This small European finch's male sports a blue-grey cap and rust-red underparts, while both sexes flash white wing bars — what species is it?
Eurasian chaffinch: Species of bird. The Eurasian chaffinch, common chaffinch, or simply the chaffinch (Fringilla coelebs) is a common and widespread small passerine bird – in the finch family.
A feathery, yellow-flowered Mediterranean herb in the carrot family, this anise-tasting plant is one of the primary ingredients in absinthe — what is it?
Fennel: Flowering plant species in the carrot family.
Named for the mathematician who used it to solve the heat equation, this expansion writes a periodic function as an infinite sum of sines and cosines — what is it?
Fourier series: Decomposition of periodic functions.
Commonly known as snails and slugs, this class is the second-largest in the animal kingdom after insects — what is it called?
Gastropod: Class of molluscs. The fossil record of gastropods extends back to the Late Cambrian.
Occurring in the cytosol, this ten-step metabolic pathway breaks glucose down into pyruvate while generating ATP and NADH — what process is it?
Glycolysis: Series of interconnected biochemical reactions.
Breeders prefer to call it a 'cavy,' and despite its name it hails from the Andes rather than West Africa and isn't related to swine at all — which Andean rodent is it?
Guinea pig: Domesticated rodent from South America.
This localized pooling of blood outside the vessels — often triggered by injury, surgery, or blood-thinning medication — starts out liquid before clotting solid within the tissue. What is it called?
Hematoma: Localized bleeding outside of blood vessels. An ecchymosis is a hematoma of the skin larger than 10 mm.
First published as a Latin anagram in 1676 by a British physicist, this principle states that the force needed to stretch a spring scales linearly with its extension — which law?
Hooke's law: Force needed to pull a spring grows linearly with distance.

Affecting roughly one in 250 baby boys, this is the second most common birth defect of the male reproductive system, in which a key opening doesn't form in its usual place — what is this condition called?
Hypospadias: Malformation in which the urethral opening is misplaced.

A former Communist Party official who was later sidelined by Nicolae Ceaușescu, this engineer-turned-politician emerged from Romania's 1989 revolution to become the country's first freely elected president — who is he?
Built from an umbrella-shaped bell of mesoglea that pulses to swim, this Cnidarian trails stinging tentacles and is the medusa phase of its complex life cycle — what is it?
Developed by a South Korean aerospace firm with Lockheed Martin and first flown in 2002, this supersonic jet trainer became the country's first indigenous supersonic aircraft — which aircraft family?
KAI T-50 Golden Eagle: Family of South Korean jet aircraft. It is South Korea's first indigenous supersonic aircraft and one of the world's few supersonic trainers.
This plant family — home to basil, rosemary, thyme, lavender, and sage — also counts teak among its rare tree species and chia among its edible seed crops — which family?
Also called May bells or Our Lady's tears, this woodland plant's sweetly scented white bell-flowers hide a dangerously poisonous secret — which flower?
Lily of the valley: Species of flowering plant in the asparagus family.
This best-known stag beetle species in Western Europe lends its genus its very name, and is currently listed as Near Threatened — what is it?
Lucanus cervus: Species of beetle. L. cervus is listed as Near Threatened by the IUCN Red List.
Sharing joints only with the temporal bones, this is the skull's lone movable bone, hosting the lower teeth and shrinking in size since humans began farming around 10,000 BCE — what is it called?
Mandible: Lower jaw bone. The mandible hosts the lower teeth (their depth delineated by the alveolar process).
Also known as flying foxes, these 197-plus species of fruit-eating bat likely evolved in Australasia some 31 million years ago — what are they called?

This medical condition, usually diagnosed shortly after birth, is defined as a length at least 2.5 standard deviations below the average and affects about 1.5 in 10,000 male newborns in North America. What is this condition?
First prepared in 1908 by biochemist Kikunae Ikeda as he tried to bottle the savory taste of kombu seaweed, this flavor enhancer is the original source of umami in cooking — what is it?
Monosodium glutamate: Flavor enhancer (621 or E621)
Native to southern Europe and North Africa, this fragrant evergreen shrub has berries that are macerated in alcohol to make Mirto liqueur — which plant?
Myrtus communis: Species of flowering plant.
This synthetic element 113 was claimed by both a Russian-American team at Dubna and, in 2004, a Japanese team at Riken. What's its name?
Nihonium: Chemical element with atomic number 113 (Nh)

Distinct from an unrelated American family with a similar name, these small seed-eating birds include house- and tree-dwelling species that nest on buildings in huge city numbers — which bird family is this?
Old World sparrow: Family of songbirds. Old World sparrows are groups of small passerine birds forming the family Passeridae.
Created by Rasmus Lerdorf in 1993, this scripting language's name began as 'Personal Home Page' before becoming a recursive backronym meaning 'Hypertext Preprocessor' — what is it?
PHP: Scripting language created in 1994. PHP is a general-purpose scripting language geared towards web development.
Often described simply as the act of teaching, this discipline studies how knowledge and skills are imparted — and how that process shapes learners socially and psychologically. What is it?
Pedagogy: Theory and practice of education.
This toxic gas, which smells like freshly cut hay, was responsible for tens of thousands of deaths as a chemical weapon in World War I — what is it?
Named after the American diplomat who introduced it from Mexico, this red-and-green Christmas plant is not actually toxic to pets — which plant?
Also known as face blindness, this cognitive disorder leaves a person unable to recognize familiar faces — even their own — while other visual skills stay intact. What is it?
Prosopagnosia: Cognitive disorder of face perception. Prosopagnosia should not be confused with prosopometamorphopsia, a disorder characterized by altered perceptions of faces.
Also known as the holly oak, this large evergreen tree native to the Mediterranean produces acorns that mature within a single summer — which species is it?
Quercus ilex: Oak tree species native to the Mediterranean.

Almost exclusively affecting girls and emerging by 18 months of age, this genetic disorder — usually caused by a mutation in the MECP2 gene — brings language and coordination loss along with repetitive hand movements. What is it?
Rett syndrome: Genetic brain disorder. Rett syndrome (RTT) is a genetic disorder that typically becomes apparent after 6–18 months of age and almost exclusively in girls.

Also called 'German measles,' this vaccine-preventable viral infection is usually mild but can cause severe birth defects — including cataracts and deafness — if a mother catches it early in pregnancy. What disease is it?
Rubella: Human viral disease. Rubella, also known as German measles or three-day measles, is a vaccine-preventable infection caused by the rubella virus.
Named after the Latin word for a small shovel, this flat triangular bone connects the upper arm bone to the collarbone and forms the back of the shoulder girdle — what is it?
Scapula: Bone that connects the humerus and clavicle.
An adult female of this ruminant is a ewe, a castrated male a wether, and a young one a lamb — and with about 1.2 billion of them, they're easily the most common of their kind. What animal?
Sheep: Domesticated ruminant bred for meat, wool, and milk.
Nicknamed a 'truth serum' in popular culture despite dubious real-world reliability, this fast-acting barbiturate anesthetic is marketed under the brand name Pentothal — which drug?
Sodium thiopental: Barbiturate general anesthetic. It is the thiobarbiturate analog of pentobarbital, and an analog of thiobarbital.
Derived from the Greek word for 'narrow,' this medical term describes the abnormal tightening of a blood vessel or other tubular structure — what is it?
Stenosis: Medical condition. Stenosis (from Ancient Greek στενός (stenós) 'narrow') is the abnormal narrowing of a blood vessel or other tubular organ or structure such as foramina and canals.

Allowing one neuron to send signals to a neighboring cell, this junction can be chemical or electrical, with coupled electrical types creating synchronized brain activity via gap junctions — what is it?
Synapse: Structure connecting neurons in the nervous system.
The primary male sex hormone, this androgen builds muscle and bone, spurs body hair, and is even linked to mood, courtship display and dominance in both sexes — what is it?
Testosterone: Primary male sex hormone. It is associated with increased aggression, sex drive, dominance, courtship display, and a wide range of behavioral characteristics.

First identified in 1846 and nicknamed 'Peter Elam's disease' in parts of South Asia, this skin condition causing patchy discoloration is caused by an overgrowth of Malassezia yeast — what is it called?
Tinea versicolor: Skin disease. Tinea versicolor (also pityriasis versicolor) is a condition characterized by a skin eruption on the trunk and proximal extremities.
One of only a few fish able to keep its body warmer than the surrounding water, this fast-swimming ocean predator's yellowfin members can reach 75 km/h — what is it?
Tuna: Tribe of fish. Tuna (pl.: tunas or tuna) is a saltwater fish that belongs to the tribe Thunnini, a subgrouping of the Scombridae (mackerel) family.
This abnormal enlargement of veins in the scrotum is the most common correctable cause of male infertility, affecting around 15% of all men — what is it called?
Varicocele: Abnormal enlargement of the pampiniform plexus veins in the scrotum.

Also known as 'wet brain,' this neurological condition results from a severe thiamine deficiency and classically presents with confusion, poor coordination, and eye movement problems — which condition is it?
Wernicke encephalopathy: Medical condition. The condition is part of a larger group of thiamine deficiency disorders that includes beriberi, in all its forms, and alcoholic Korsakoff syndrome.

What is the chemical symbol for bromine?
The symbol for bromine is Br. Bromine is a chemical element; it has symbol Br and atomic number 35.
Tantalum is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for tantalum is Ta. Tantalum is a chemical element; it has symbol Ta and atomic number 73.
